keyVerseText: And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah.
rootMeaning: The root of מֹלֶכֶת (Môleketh) is מָלַךְ (mâlak), which means to reign, rule, or be king or queen. As a feminine active participle, מֹלֶכֶת literally signifies one who reigns or rules—a queen. This root sense emphasizes authority and sovereignty, going beyond the English gloss of 'queen' by highlighting the active role of reigning and governing, which is inherent in the Hebrew term.
usageInScripture: The word מֹלֶכֶת appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 7:18, where it is used as a proper name, Hammoleketh, referring to an Israelite woman. The top translation reflects this unique usage as a proper name rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence indicates that while the term can mean 'queen,' here it primarily identifies a person, showing the flexibility of the term in Hebrew to function both as a title and a personal name.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מֹלֶכֶת as rooted in the concept of reigning enriches our appreciation of biblical authority and divine sovereignty. It reminds believers that leadership and rulership are roles ordained by God, reflecting His own kingship. The fact that this term is used as a personal name highlights how identity in Scripture can be intertwined with divine roles and purposes. For the Christian faith, it underscores the truth that all authority ultimately points to Christ, the King of kings, and invites believers to recognize the significance of godly rule both in history and in their spiritual lives.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 7:18, 'And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah,' the name Hammoleketh identifies a woman within the genealogy of Manasseh. The use of מֹלֶכֶת here as a personal name rather than a title invites reflection on the legacy and heritage of those who bear names connected to divine kingship. It subtly conveys the presence of God-ordained authority and blessing within the family line, reminding readers that God's sovereign rule extends through His people.
